tagline: North from the gold town, beside a drowned stage stop.
intro: From Weaverville, the Trinity Heritage route takes Highway 3 toward Trinity Center, following the shore of Trinity Lake before continuing into the mountains. Weaverville’s Gold Rush history includes a Chinese temple where worship continues; the old Trinity Center took a different course.
That stage-stop town now lies beneath the reservoir. Southwest of the present town, the Bowerman Barn keeps another part of the mining country's economy: the ranches that fed it.

moments.title: Weaverville Joss House
moments.text: A guardian lion stolen from the temple in 1934 came back in 1989, left in a box at the visitor center.

moments.title: Bowerman Barn
moments.text: Jacob Bowerman built this barn by hand from whipsawn pine, part of a ranch supplying beef and dairy products to the mining country.

moments.title: Trinity Center
moments.text: Trinity Center's I.O.O.F. building was among the handful moved from the old 1851 stage stop before Trinity Lake covered it.
